\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{آب} \fa{و} \fa{هوا} (âb-o havâ)}{آب و هوا (âb-o havâ)}]{\fa{آب} \fa{و} \fa{هوا} (âb-o havâ) — the climate; the weather}

\label{lesson:FA-C473-ab-o-hava}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for a volcano, then the Persian for a habitat.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{آب} \fa{و} \fa{هوا}}
\textbf{\fa{آب} \fa{و} \fa{هوا}} (\emph{âb-o havâ}) — \textquotedblleft{}the climate; the weather\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{آب} \fa{و} \fa{هوای} \fa{شمال} \fa{مرطوب} \fa{است}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Âb-o havâ-ye shomâl martub ast.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The climate in the north is humid.
\end{quote}

Literally 'water and air'.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{âb-o havâ} is listed in EtymDB as 'water and air': native \emph{âb} 'water', from Middle Persian \emph{āb}, joined with \emph{havâ} 'air', borrowed from Arabic \emph{hawāʾ}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{âb-o havâ}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{âb-o havâ}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{âb-o havâ}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for a volcano, then the Persian for a habitat, then say \emph{âb-o havâ} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \fa{آب} \fa{و} \fa{هوا} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}The climate; the weather\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{هواشناسی} (havâshenâsi)}{هواشناسی (havâshenâsi)}]{\fa{هواشناسی} (havâshenâsi) — the weather service; meteorology}

\label{lesson:FA-C473-havashenasi}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for a habitat, then the Persian for the climate.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{هواشناسی}}
\textbf{\fa{هواشناسی}} (\emph{havâshenâsi}) — \textquotedblleft{}the weather service; meteorology\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{هواشناسی} \fa{برای} \fa{فردا} \fa{باران} \fa{اعلام} \fa{کرد}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Havâshenâsi barâ-ye fardâ bârân e'lâm kard.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The weather service forecast rain for tomorrow.
\end{quote}

\emph{havâ} 'air' + \emph{shenâsi} 'knowing, the study of'.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{havâshenâsi} is built from \emph{havâ} 'air', borrowed from Arabic \emph{hawāʾ} (EtymDB), and native \emph{shenâsi} 'knowing, the study of', from \emph{shenâkhtan} 'to know'.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{درجه} (daraje)}{درجه (daraje)}]{\fa{درجه} (daraje) — a degree (of temperature); a grade}

\label{lesson:FA-C473-daraje}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for the climate, then the Persian for the weather service.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{درجه}}
\textbf{\fa{درجه}} (\emph{daraje}) — \textquotedblleft{}a degree (of temperature); a grade\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{امروز} \fa{دمای} \fa{هوا} \fa{سی} \fa{درجه} \fa{است}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Emruz damâ-ye havâ si daraje ast.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Today the temperature is thirty degrees.
\end{quote}

\emph{Daraje-ye yek} — first class.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{daraje} was borrowed from Arabic \emph{daraja} 'a step, a degree' (EtymDB).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{daraje}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{daraje}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for the climate, then the Persian for the weather service, then say \emph{daraje} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{تغییر} \fa{کردن} (taghyir kardan)}{تغییر کردن (taghyir kardan)}]{\fa{تغییر} \fa{کردن} (taghyir kardan) — to change}

\label{lesson:FA-C473-taghyir-kardan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for the weather service, then the Persian for a degree.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{تغییر} \fa{کردن}}
\textbf{\fa{تغییر} \fa{کردن}} (\emph{taghyir kardan}) — \textquotedblleft{}to change\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{هوا} \fa{ناگهان} \fa{تغییر} \fa{کرد}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Havâ nâgahân taghyir kard.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The weather suddenly changed.
\end{quote}

Intransitive: the thing changes. \emph{Taghyir dâdan} is to change something.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{taghyir kardan} is built from \emph{taghyir} 'change', borrowed from Arabic \emph{taġyīr} (EtymDB), and \emph{kardan} 'to do', inherited from Middle Persian \emph{kardan} (EtymDB).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for the weather service, then the Persian for a degree, then say \emph{taghyir kardan} again

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{زیر} \fa{صفر} (zir-e sefr)}{زیر صفر (zir-e sefr)}]{\fa{زیر} \fa{صفر} (zir-e sefr) — below zero (of temperature)}

\label{lesson:FA-C473-zir-e-sefr}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for a degree, then the Persian for to change.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{زیر} \fa{صفر}}
\textbf{\fa{زیر} \fa{صفر}} (\emph{zir-e sefr}) — \textquotedblleft{}below zero (of temperature)\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{دیشب} \fa{دما} \fa{ده} \fa{درجه} \fa{زیر} \fa{صفر} \fa{بود}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Dishab damâ dah daraje zir-e sefr bud.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Last night it was ten degrees below zero.
\end{quote}

\emph{zir} 'under' + \emph{sefr} 'zero'.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{zir-e sefr} is built from native \emph{zir} 'under' and \emph{sefr} 'zero', borrowed from Arabic \emph{ṣifr} 'nothing, cipher' (EtymDB). EtymDB traces English \emph{zero} to the same Arabic word.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for a degree, then the Persian for to change, then say \emph{zir-e sefr} again
